title: Mental Illness And Substance Use Disorder Medications
subtopic: Mental illness and substance use disorder medications
rule_summary: Massachusetts guidance permits appropriately trained pharmacists and pharmacy interns to administer listed patient-specific prescribed single-dose long-acting mental-health medications and extended-release naltrexone under specified conditions. Required safeguards include patient-specific prescribing, training/CPR, counseling, recordkeeping and privacy. Routine pharmacist-prescriber communication and sending administration records as soon as practical are strongly encouraged; adverse events should be communicated within 24 hours, and specified serious outcomes must be reported to the prescriber immediately.
exam_relevance: Tests a distinct pharmacist decision path using current official authority rather than rote trivia.

authority.name: Massachusetts Drug Control Program — Circular DCP 19-2-105
authority.section: Dispensing by Administration; Record Keeping; Reporting Adverse Events; Pharmacist-Prescriber Communication; Privacy

common_confusions: Routine administration-record transmission to the prescriber is strongly encouraged rather than a categorical prerequisite to every administration; specified serious adverse events have an immediate reporting requirement.
verification_notes: Repaired after independent Batch 2 audit PR #36 / adjudication Issue #37 to distinguish strongly encouraged routine communication from adverse-event reporting duties. Requires fresh independent re-audit before release.
